objective.value: Develop a GalP/Glk-dependent, PTS-defective Escherichia coli L-tryptophan producer with higher yield and specific productivity by combining rational engineering (ptsI knockout, galP/glk promoter engineering, integration of AroG^D6G-D7A and AnTrpC^R378F variants) with batch and continuous adaptive laboratory evolution using an automatic CRISPR/Cas9-facilitated growth-coupled sensor-guided screening system (auto-CGSS).
objective.notes: Primary research objective stated in abstract and final Introduction paragraph.

hypothesis.value: Replacing PTS glucose uptake with the PTS-independent GalP/Glk system increases phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) availability and can theoretically raise the maximum Trp yield from 0.227 g/g (PTS) to 0.454 g/g; growth impairment of PTS-defective strains can be overcome by modulated galP/glk expression and evolution.
hypothesis.notes: Stoichiometric/theoretical-yield reasoning (Fig. S1) plus literature proposal that PEP availability limits Trp yield.

strain.value: E. coli Trp producer S028 (parental, previously constructed by Chen and Zeng 2017) and derivatives constructed/used here: S028TS/pCas9 (Ptac-tnaC-eGFP biosensor integrated), G028 (ΔptsI), G028Δglk::CmR (G028Cm), G028Cm/pJC184/pCas9MT (G028JC), promoter-mutant pool G028a, reference G028GG (non-mutated ptac-galP-pJ23119-glk), batch-ALE strain K3, phase-1 continuous-evolution strain G028c, final evolved strain T5, and enzyme-variant integrants T5AA and S028AA; E. coli Top10 used as cloning host; E. coli W3110 used as WGS reference.
strain.notes: Full strain/plasmid genotypes are in Supplementary Table S1 (not available): strain reconstruction blocked_pending_supplement. W3110 inferred as likely lineage background of S028 because it is the WGS reference and rational-design variants are annotated against it, but the paper does not explicitly state S028's parent in the main text.

genotype.value: S028TS/pCas9: chromosomal Ptac-tnaC-eGFP Trp biosensor in S028/pCas9. G028: ΔptsI. G028Cm: glk promoter region (-50 to 0 bp) replaced by CmR. Promoter mutants: randomized -10/-35 regions of synthetic ptac-galP and pJ23119-glk cassettes chromosomally integrated. T5 (vs W3110 reference): 15 modified and 5 deleted genes incl. galP K137T/P195A/F204L, zwf Glu165Stop, mlc(dgsA) deletion, plus rationally designed aroG S180F, serA H344A/N364A, trpE S40F, rpsL K43R inherited from lineage. T5AA/S028AA: chromosomal integration of aroG^D6G-D7A and AntrpC^R378F.
genotype.notes: Table 2 is OCR-garbled (row misalignment); mutation list should be verified against the published PDF/Supplement. Complete genotypes require Supplementary Table S1.

engineering_method.value: CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing (ptsI knockout, biosensor integration, promoter cassette integration, plasmid curing); in vitro random mutagenesis of galP/glk promoter -10/-35 elements (PCR-based, DpnI, fusion, Top10 library pCmN20-GGMT); CGSS (growth-coupled + Trp biosensor-guided in vivo screening); batch-mode ALE of 12 mutants; continuous ALE in a 30 mL auxostat (auto-CGSS) combining pJC184 mutagenesis plasmid (arabinose-induced mutators), real-time OD and online flow-cytometric Trp-fluorescence monitoring; homology modeling (Modeller) and docking (AutoDock Vina) for GalP variant analysis.
engineering_method.notes: CGSS approach itself was developed in a previous paper (Chen et al., 2019) - background method, adapted here.

value: E1: G028 growth/glucose-utilization test in M9+glucose (60 h)
E2: 84 promoter mutants in 96-deep-well M9 + controls (S028 H1-H6; G028GG H7-H12)
E3: 12 selected promoter mutants + S028 batch fermentation in FM-III (50 mL tubes)
E4: batch ALE of 12 mutants -> K3; fed-batch K3 vs S028
E5: continuous auto-CGSS evolution (two phases 0-380 h, 381-550 h); 6 phase-1 samples; 20 colonies each from 4 phase-2 time points + controls S028/K3/G028c; 10 high-MFU mutants in FM-III shake flasks
E6: fed-batch T5 vs S028 (plasmid-free T5)
E8: WGS of T5 vs W3110 + PCR resequencing of galP/zwf/mlc in T5 and S028
E9: GalP homology modeling/docking (K137T, P195A, F204L)
experimental_groups.notes: Groups are instantiated per experiment; no paper-level unified design exists.

time.value: G028 M9 growth test ~60 h; deep-well fluorescence assay 10 h; shake-flask mutant characterization 20-24 h; continuous evolution phase 1: 0-380 h (fluorescence peak ~11,446 MFU at 126 h), phase 2: 381-550 h (peak ~13,541 MFU at ~390-438 h), colony sampling at 462 h etc.; fed-batch 65 h (yield compared at 50 h for K3); SynM agar 30 h colony growth.
time.notes: One continuous-ALE campaign with two sequential phases; not a single-time-point selection.

replicates.value: Screening heat maps and shake-flask characterizations: 'two independent biological samples' (Fig. 1 and Fig. 5 captions); fed-batch fermentations: means+SD from 'two independent measurements'; fluorescence: MFI of 10,000 events per sample; 20 single colonies per evolution sample.
replicates.notes: n=2 biological replicates; 'two independent measurements' for fed-batch is ambiguous between technical and biological replication (replicate_type unresolved for bioreactor runs). No statistical tests reported; only SD.

assay.value: OD600 growth; Trp-biosensor eGFP fluorescence (MFU; ex 488 nm / em 509 nm; electronic gating vs PBS background); Trp quantification by sensitive spectrophotometric method (Nagaraja et al. 2003); glucose, shikimate (SA), 3-dehydroshikimate (DSA) by HPLC; pyruvate tracked in Fig. 2F (method not restated); WGS (BGISEQ) + PCR resequencing of key mutations.
assay.notes: Biosensor reports intracellular Trp indirectly via fluorescence; not a direct Trp assay.

instruments.value: Ultrospec 10 cell density meter (Biochrom); CytoFLEX flow cytometer (Beckman Coulter); DASGIP 4-parallel 1.5 L bioreactor system (Julich); BGISEQ sequencer (BGI); HPLC (model not specified); electroporator (0.2 cm cuvette, 2.5 kV).

analysis_methods.value: Beckman Flow software with electronic gating (MFU); SOAPdenovo v1.05 assembly; SNP calling with MUMmer + BLAT; BLAST confirmation; InDel detection with LASTZ verified by BWA + samtools; homology modeling Modeller v9.24 (template STP10 PDB 6H7D); PyMoL structural alignment; AutoDock Vina docking in Chimera; stoichiometric theoretical-yield analysis (Fig. S1).
analysis_methods.notes: No formal statistical hypothesis testing reported; comparisons stated as percent differences with SD.

outcomes.value: G028: severe growth defect (OD600 0.21±0.02 after 60 h from 0.10). Promoter screen: 12/84 mutants with growth >1.25 + high MFU; 4 (D10, E12, F8, G1) best in FM-III but below S028. Batch ALE strain K3: yield 0.137 g/g (< S028 0.150), restored late growth, glucose uptake 4.10 g/L/h (40-50 h), lower shikimate, ~5x higher pyruvate (2.95 g/L); no mutations in galP/glk/galR. Continuous auto-CGSS strain T5: yield 0.164 g/g (+9.33% vs S028, +19.71% vs K3), Trp 38.77 g/L, qTrp 25.28 mg/gDCW/h (+45% vs S028), biomass 32% lower. T5AA: yield 0.195 g/g, Trp 41.49 g/L, qTrp 28.83 mg/gDCW/h; S028AA: 0.185 g/g, 48.27 g/L, qTrp 23.74, Vp 0.77 > T5AA 0.67. T5 genomics: 15 modified + 5 deleted genes incl. mlc deletion, zwf E165Stop, galP K137T/P195A/F204L. Yields remain below theoretical maxima (0.227/0.454 g/g); SA/DSA still accumulate.
outcomes.notes: Mechanistic links (mlc derepression -> PEP, GalP mutations -> transport, zwf stop -> growth/NADPH effects) are author hypotheses requiring confirmation - inference, not validated causality.

experiments.purpose: Create PTS-defective Trp producer to redirect PEP from glucose uptake into Trp biosynthesis
experiments.host: E. coli S028TS/pCas9 (S028 + chromosomal Ptac-tnaC-eGFP biosensor)
experiments.intervention: CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of ptsI (PTS Enzyme I) -> strain G028; growth evaluated in M9 + glucose, 60 h
experiments.conditions: LB overnight, wash x3 M9, M9 glucose sole carbon source, initial OD600 0.10
experiments.control: Parental S028 context (functional PTS) as benchmark in subsequent experiments
experiments.outcome: G028 reached only OD600 0.21±0.02 after ~60 h; glucose uptake/growth severely blocked

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 active ptsI knockout by authors; Q2 performed in this paper; Q3 created the chassis whose phenotype drove all subsequent promoter engineering and evolution.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: PTS removal spares PEP (precursor/reducing-power supply for the Trp pathway) rather than modifying the product pathway itself.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Stoichiometric analysis: PTS consumes 1 mol PEP per mol glucose, capping theoretical Trp yield at 0.227 g/g; >80% of PEP could be freed in a PTS-defective GalP/Glk strain (theoretical 0.454 g/g).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Chemical-stoichiometry-based theoretical yield plus measured growth phenotype of the knockout.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper explicitly explains the PEP-consumption mechanism of PTS and its coupling to Trp precursor supply.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When producing PEP-dependent aromatics such as L-tryptophan in E. coli, apply PTS inactivation with a PTS-independent glucose uptake route (GalP/Glk), because PTS consumes one PEP per internalized glucose and its removal frees PEP for product biosynthesis.
alternatives_considered: Glf (Z. mobilis)/Glk and GalP/Glk activation cited as alternative glucose-uptake restorations (literature background, not tested here)

experiments.purpose: Build host enabling CRISPR/Cas9-facilitated promoter engineering of galP/glk
experiments.intervention: Replace glk promoter -50..0 bp with chloramphenicol resistance gene CmR to provide sgRNA target and selection marker -> G028Δglk::CmR (G028Cm)
experiments.conditions: CRISPR/Cas9 editing; details delegated to Supplement

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 deliberate genome edit; Q2 done in this work; Q3 enables the subsequent promoter-library integration/screening workflow.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Construction of the screening-enabling chassis for integrated selection.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Need for an sgRNA target sequence at the glk locus to apply CRISPR/Cas9 promoter replacement.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Physical construction with antibiotic selection; construction itself is measured, downstream function tested in E3.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper states the explicit functional logic (CmR provides sgRNA target + selection marker); a technical-mechanistic rationale rather than literature analogy.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When performing CRISPR/Cas9-mediated chromosomal promoter replacement in E. coli, first insert an antibiotic-resistance marker at the target locus, because it simultaneously provides selection and a unique sgRNA target for the subsequent library swap.

experiments.purpose: Recover glucose utilization/growth of the PTS-defective strain by modulated galP/glk expression
experiments.intervention: Random mutagenesis of -10/-35 elements of ptac-galP and pJ23119-glk cassette (plasmid library pCmN20-GGMT), CRISPR/Cas9 chromosomal integration, growth-coupled + Trp-biosensor screening (CGSS): 84 mutants in 96-deep-well M9, then 12 mutants in FM-III batch
experiments.conditions: M9 deep-well screen; FM-III, 50 mL conical tubes, 37 C 250 rpm; 10 h assay
experiments.control: S028 positive control (H1-H6); G028GG non-mutated synthetic promoters reference (H7-H12)
experiments.readout: OD600 and MFU heat maps; batch fermentation growth/MFU
experiments.outcome: 12 mutants with growth >1.25 and high MFU; D10/E12/F8/G1 best in FM-III but still below S028

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 promoter engineering action; Q2 done in this paper; Q3 screen outcome (mutants still inferior) triggered batch ALE.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Combinatorial promoter tuning to balance galP/glk expression levels.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: ptsI knockout strain G028 showed near-zero growth in M9+glucose (OD 0.21 after 60 h), i.e. native galP/glk expression insufficient to restore glucose uptake.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured screen and fermentation readouts for 84/12 mutants.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Beneficial promoter variants arose from random mutagenesis plus screening, not from a stated mechanistic prediction of specific sequences.

experiments.purpose: Further improve GalP/Glk-dependent strain by batch adaptive evolution
experiments.intervention: Batch-mode ALE campaign (details in Supplementary Materials); best strain K3 evaluated by fed-batch vs S028; galP/glk/galR sequenced
experiments.conditions: fed-batch DASGIP, 500 mL start, initial glucose 25 g/L, OD600 0.45, 65 h
experiments.readout: growth, Trp, yield, qTrp, glucose uptake, shikimate, pyruvate; Sanger sequencing of galP/glk/galR
experiments.outcome: K3 yield 0.137 g/g (< S028 0.150 at 50 h); growth restored after 30 h; glucose uptake 4.10 g/L/h (40-50 h); pyruvate 2.95 g/L (~5x S028); lower shikimate; no galP/glk/galR mutations

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 ALE campaign initiated by authors; Q2 in this paper; Q3 K3's failure to improve yield (and pyruvate-overflow observation) motivated building the continuous auto-CGSS system.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Selection/evolution campaign as an integrated screening step.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Best promoter mutants (D10/E12/F8/G1) still grew and produced below S028 in FM-III batch fermentation.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Fed-batch measurements of the evolved strain.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: K3 was obtained by adaptive evolution/selection; the route of improvement was not rationally specified.

experiments.purpose: Obtain a higher-yield GalP/Glk-dependent Trp producer via automated continuous evolution
experiments.host: E. coli G028Cm/pJC184/pCas9MT (G028JC) with chromosomal promoter library
experiments.intervention: Continuous auxostat evolution (auto-CGSS): pJC184 arabinose-induced in vivo mutagenesis, OD600 held at 0.8 via automated inlet/outlet pumps (60-80 mL/h, 30 mL vessel), online flow-cytometric Trp fluorescence; two phases (0-380 h, 381-550 h) with G028c as phase-1 winner; colony screening and FM-III characterization -> T5
experiments.conditions: SynM + 15 ug/mL Cm + 25 ug/mL Kan + arabinose, 30 C; colonies on SynM agar 30 h; FM-III shake flasks 20 h
experiments.control: S028, K3, G028c as positive/reference controls in colony characterization
experiments.replicates: two independent biological samples (screens); 20 colonies per sample
experiments.readout: real-time OD600 + MFU; offline growth/MFU; batch fermentation
experiments.outcome: Phase peaks ~11,446 MFU (126 h) and ~13,541 MFU (390-438 h) followed by decline (growth-over-production drift); 10 mutants with MFU >10,000; T5 best in FM-III and selected for fed-batch

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 new engineered evolution system + campaign; Q2 built and run in this paper (adapting their prior CGSS); Q3 produced T5 and defined the subsequent variant-integration step.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Integrated mutagenesis-selection-monitoring platform (auto-CGSS) as an integrated screening design.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Batch-ALE strain K3 increased glucose uptake but not Trp yield and accumulated ~5x pyruvate, suggesting evolution favored growth pathways over Trp; a sensor-guided continuous selection was needed to keep selection on productivity.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Real-time measured evolution trajectories and offline fermentation characterization.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: T5's improvements emerged from random genome-context mutagenesis and selection; specific beneficial mutations were not pre-designed.

experiments.purpose: Stabilize T5 genotype and evaluate production performance
experiments.intervention: Remove mutagenesis plasmid pJC184 via IPTG-inducible Cas9MT retargeted to CmR (sgRNA-pMB1 -> sgRNA-CmR), then fed-batch of plasmid-free T5 vs S028
experiments.conditions: DASGIP fed-batch 65 h, initial glucose 25 g/L, OD600 0.45
experiments.readout: OD600, DCW, Trp, qTrp, yield, Vp, SA, DSA

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 deliberate plasmid-curing modification; Q2 in this paper; Q3 stabilized strain enabled all downstream fermentation and variant integration.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Genotypic stabilization as part of fermentation/process execution.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: pJC184 mutagenesis plasmid would cause undesired continuing mutations during fermentation.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured fed-batch performance of the cured strain.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Explicit causal reasoning: an active mutator plasmid would keep mutating the production strain during evaluation.

experiments.purpose: Further raise Trp yield by strengthening downstream/limiting enzymatic steps
experiments.intervention: Chromosomal integration of previously engineered variants aroG^D6G-D7A and AntrpC^R378F into T5 (-> T5AA) and S028 (-> S028AA); comparative fed-batch
experiments.control: S028AA vs T5AA; comparison to T5 and S028
experiments.readout: growth, Trp, glucose, yield, qTrp, Vp
experiments.outcome: T5AA yield 0.195 g/g (+18.90% vs T5, +5.41% vs S028AA), Trp 41.49 g/L, qTrp 28.83; S028AA higher final titer (48.27 g/L) and Vp (0.77 vs 0.67) due to better growth

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 new chromosomal integrations performed here; Q2 integration done in this paper (variants themselves from prior work); Q3 results redefine the best strain and next targets (biomass limitation).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Introduction of superior enzyme variants at rate-limiting pathway steps (DAHP synthase, anthranilate-activated AnTrpC).
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: T5 yield still far below theoretical maximum and SA/DSA intermediates accumulated, indicating downstream pathway limitation.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured fed-batch outcomes of the integrants.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Both variants were previously engineered and validated (Chen et al. 2018, 2019) and were adopted off-the-shelf; no new mechanistic design rationale is given in this paper.
